items.heading: "Switch to Non
items.text: "Switch to non-IT" gets treated online like a single leap. It is actually several distinct doors, each asking for a different credential, a different network, and a different amount of patience before it pays what you are used to. If your goal is to stay close to tech but move into a management or product lane, read the dedicated career switch from IT to management guide instead, the guidance below covers doors that take you genuinely outside the tech industry.

items.heading: Nobody Starting From Zero
items.text: Nobody starting from zero. Years in IT build a specific stack of habits that most people undervalue, because they assume "transferable skill" means something abstract like "problem solving." It is more specific than that, and it maps differently onto each door.

columns: What it means for your decision
rows: ~68% of Indian IT professionals show 2+ clinical burnout indicators (NASSCOM-Deloitte, 2025)
The exhaustion driving this search is a real, shared industry pattern, not a personal weakness or overreaction.
58% of Indian professionals 35+ have considered a mid-career change in the last 2 years; only ~12% act on it
Wanting out is common. The gap between wanting and doing is usually a missing test plan, not a missing reason.
400,000-500,000 mid-career IT roles projected for restructuring by 2028 (NASSCOM)
Waiting indefinitely for the "right moment" carries its own risk if your current role sits in a legacy-heavy function.
UPSC CSE 2025: ~958 selected out of ~5.8 lakh who appeared (roughly 0.1-0.2% success)
Government-exam doors are real, but treating one exam as your only fallback plan is a genuine financial risk.

items.heading: Build or Confirm an Emergency
items.text: Build or confirm an emergency fund covering at least 6-12 months of full household expenses before you resign for a door with an unpredictable early income (entrepreneurship, freelancing, exam prep with no fallback job).

items.heading: If You Are Financing
items.text: If you are financing a course or exam-prep coaching with savings or a loan, write the actual monthly cost against your realistic post-switch income, not the best-case story from an advertisement.

items.heading: Separate "I Am Changing Fields"
items.text: Separate "I am changing fields" from "I am also taking on new financial risk", doing both fully at once multiplies your risk instead of just adding it.
